conviction_note: No company-level unpriced number found; a direct peer (Cars.com, today) shows US dealer counts still slipping and revenue below consensus, a brand-new CFO sets his first Q4 guide, against a short book that grew 70% Aug-Oct to ~12.6% of Class A shares and calls bid at -25 skew; the stock has already run +22% in 20 sessions and ~+6% today in sympathy with Cars.com's +10%, so the evidence offsets and p_up sits at 49 on a 10% abs move (set below the 13.5% indicative implied move, whose ATM spread is 76% of mid, and above the 7.3% median reaction).
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $256.4-256.5M (MarketBeat 2026-10-29 consensus $256.46M, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-cargurus-carg-set-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-thursday-2026-10-29/ ; Benzinga $256.4M via search snippet) = midpoint of company guide $253.5-258.5M; non-GAAP EPS consensus $0.664 vs guide $0.63-0.69; adj. EBITDA guide $82-90M (company release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001494259/000119312526338014/carg-ex99_1.htm, 2026-08-06). Q4 revenue consensus ~$263.4M (Benzinga, August-dated, possibly stale); FY2026 guide +10-13% revenue, adj. EBITDA margin down 50-150bp. Bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest 9,492,243 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up from 7,729,497 (09-30), 7,226,663 (09-15), 6,386,305 (08-31) and 5,590,737 (08-14): +70% in two months; 10.7% of total shares outstanding and ~12.6% of the 75.3M Class A shares; days to cover 5.03 (https://equibles.com/stocks/carg/shortinterest, read 2026-11-05; 10-30 settlement not yet published). Borrow fee ~0.4% (curvedtrading snippet). Baseline skew_25d = -25.42 vol points (calls richer than puts: 'upside paid'); put/call OI ratio field reads 79.83, which looks mis-scaled; ATM spread 76% of mid so the 13.52% event-implied move is indicative only. Run-up +22.3% over 20 days and +10.0% over 5 days, from $28.77 on 2026-10-07 to $35.76 sealed intraday, 8.4% below the 52w high. Much of the short was added near the lows (~$29-31), so part of the 20-day rally is plausibly covering already done.

findings.finding: Cars.com, the closest US listed peer, reported Q3 2026 this morning: dealer customers 19,251, down from 19,343 in Q2 (-0.5% q/q) and 19,526 a year ago (-1% y/y); revenue $181.9M vs ~$183.2M consensus (a miss); dealer revenue +1%, marketplace revenue +5% y/y; ARPD +3%; traffic -4% y/y; release cites 'current market conditions' pressuring dealer media products; but EBITDA margin 30.7% beat and CARS traded ~+10% on the day, and CARG rose ~6% today in sympathy. For CARG, the bar is US paying dealers (26,151 in Q2, +3% y/y) and QARSD; a peer losing dealers q/q says dealer spend was still cautious in Q3, matching CARG's own Q2 warning of a more measured pace of dealer decisions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CARG fell -8.95% on the 2026-05-07 print, when dealer caution was first flagged, and then slid ~28% over ten sessions (Trefis 2026-05-21/22); it rose +7.16% on 2026-08-06 when revenue beat and EBITDA guide was above consensus despite a below-consensus revenue guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Released a few hours before CARG's print; the market read it positively (CARS ~+10% on margin, CARG ~+6% in sympathy), so the dealer-count softness is the part being looked through. If the dealer read were priced as a negative for CARG, CARG would not have rallied with CARS today.
findings.independence: Cox Automotive Q3 2026 Dealer Sentiment Index: market outlook 46, second straight quarterly decline, down from 53 a year earlier (https://www.coxautoinc.com/press-releases/q3-2026-cadsi-dealer-sentiment-weakens-as-new-vehicle-sales-outlook-slips/) - filed separately as a proxy. Revenue-miss vs consensus confirmed by https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/carscom-earnings-beat-by-005-revenue-fell-short-of-estimates-5003878 (same release).

findings.finding: Short interest in CARG rose from 5.59M shares (Aug 14) to 9.49M (Oct 15), ~12.6% of Class A shares and 5.0 days to cover, while the stock then rallied +22% in 20 sessions to $35.76 and the option market prices calls over puts by 25 vol points; an in-line or better print with an acceptable Q4 guide meets a short book largely built at $29-31 that is now under water.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CARG print with a short book of this size was found; reactions to the last eight prints range -17.1% to +11.2% with 4 of 7 up, so outcome tails are wide both ways.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the -25 skew and the 22% run-up are what a market leaning to a squeeze looks like, so this is sized small. What is not visible in the price is how much of the 9.5M was covered in the rally; the 10-30 settlement is unpublished, and the model estimate (9.83M) suggests little covering.
findings.independence: Sep 30 figure 7.73M / 5.5 DTC from a separate snippet (curvedtrading.com) agrees with the series; skew from the sealed baseline (independent of short data).

findings.finding: Cox Automotive's Q3 2026 Dealer Sentiment Index fell to 46 on market outlook, the second straight quarterly decline and down from 53 a year earlier, with independents more pessimistic than franchised dealers and affordability/borrowing costs cited, while independents' profit index rose 3 to 36 and September used retail sales ran +2% y/y with 49 days' supply (Cox, September 2026 inventory).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific; the May 2026 print fell -8.95% on dealer caution, which this series is a proxy for.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (Q3 2026 CADSI, URL path /2026/09/ on the PDF)
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series, likely in analyst models; filed as a proxy because CarGurus' revenue is dealer subscription spend and the company itself flagged a measured pace of dealer decisions for Q3. Mixed: used retail volume +2% y/y and better independent profits cut the other way.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Cox September 2026 used inventory note: https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/used-vehicle-inventory-september-2026/ (same publisher). Cars.com dealer-count decline (finding 1) points the same way from a different source.

findings.finding: The Q4 2026 guide (and any 2027 framing) will be set by a new CFO, Matthew Mandel, who started on 2026-10-19 (ex-CFO/COO of Fleetio), 17 days before the print; CEO Trevisan had been interim principal financial officer. Q4 consensus revenue ~$263.4M (+~9% y/y) sits in the upper half of the implied FY range; a first guide from an incoming CFO is a guidance-scale event that the market cannot see until tonight.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has driven CARG reactions: May 2026 margin/dealer guide -8.95%; Aug 2026 revenue guide slightly below consensus but EBITDA guide above, +7.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointment is public; the inference that a new CFO guides conservatively is not company-confirmed, so this is sized small. If the market expected a cautious Q4 guide, the stock would not have run 22% into the print with calls bid.

findings.finding: New York City's DCWP sued CarGurus in NY Supreme Court on 2026-10-15 alleging >2,000 Consumer Protection Law violations, chiefly 'Great/Good Deal' ratings that ignore mandatory dealer fees and an AI chatbot listing deals without fees; it seeks an injunction and civil penalties. Penalties look small relative to ~$1B revenue, but a forced change to how Deal Ratings treat fees touches the core dealer product and may be asked about on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stock was ~$30.3 on 2026-10-16 and rallied ~18% afterwards, so the market has so far looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced (public three weeks, stock up since). Residual is only whether management discloses a product or reserve change tonight.

findings.finding: A third-party AI-answer visibility index shows CarGurus' 'valid recommendation coverage' across AI/search answers falling from 89.1% (July 2026) to 86.0% (October 2026), while Cars.com's Q3 release claims it is now the #1 most-cited automotive marketplace across major LLMs; AI disintermediation is the main bear thesis cited by the market (stock was ~11x EPS at $29 in mid-October).
findings.why_not_priced: Obscure series with 738 observations; it does not reach revenue in the quarter. Sized near zero: matters only if management's AI-traffic commentary (Discover, ChatGPT app) disappoints.
findings.independence: Cars.com Q3 release LLM-citation claim (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001683606/000119312526448613/cars-ex99_1.htm); bear-case framing in https://investresearch.substack.com/p/cargurus-carg-the-auto-trader-of (2026-10-13, author long).

findings.finding: Insider selling into the print is routine plan selling: COO Samuel Zales sold 10,000 shares and CPO sold 1,964 on 2026-11-02 at $32.33 under 10b5-1 plans, and the Langley Steinert Irrevocable Family Trust (founder, 10% holder) filed a Form 144 for 100,000 Class A shares (~$3.38M) on 2026-11-04 under a plan adopted 2026-05-29.
findings.why_not_priced: Plans adopted months ago, small versus 89M shares; carries no information on the quarter. Filed at 0 for completeness.

findings.finding: Capital return capacity: the 2026 buyback had ~$46M left after Q2 ($75M remaining at 3/31 less $29.4M bought in Q2), cash was $122M at 6/30 after $206M of H1 buybacks, and the revolver was resized to $200M through 2031 with an incremental facility of the greater of $380M or 100% of trailing EBITDA; a new authorization with the Q3 print is plausible given ~11-12% FCF yield and >30% share-count reduction since 2022.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior: buyback news has accompanied prints in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference: no announcement exists; the revolver amendment (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1494259/000119312526338014/carg-20260806.htm) is financing that buys flexibility rather than signalling distress (leverage covenant 6.25x, no debt drawn disclosed).
findings.independence: Substack 2026-10-13 reports >$200M repurchased in H1 at ~$32.50 average (https://investresearch.substack.com/p/cargurus-carg-the-auto-trader-of).

outside_window.finding: NYC DCWP lawsuit outcome (injunction on Deal Ratings fee treatment, civil penalties) will be decided in court long after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The skew (calls bid at -25) and the 22% run-up lean up, and the crowded short agrees with them; the dealer-side evidence (Cars.com dealer count down q/q, revenue miss, Cox sentiment down) and a new CFO's first guide cut mildly against, so overall the evidence roughly offsets and the run-up has already taken much of the upside the skew pays for.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short is a mechanism against a negative; sign against strong skew needs a reason): shrank the Cars.com dealer read-through from -0.5 to -0.4 and the new-CFO guide inference from -0.5 to -0.3; applied once each.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism' plus lesson 7: moved p_up from 48 to 49, expected_move from -0.4 to -0.2.
Lesson 5 (proxies filed small, not dropped): Cox CADSI and the AI-visibility index stay at -0.3 and -0.2; unchanged.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest of the company): the dealer read-through is US-only; international (~10% of revenue, dealers +11%, QARSD +11% in Q2) is the offset, already reflected in the -0.4 size.
Lesson 6: bar verified against company guide midpoint plus two agreeing estimates; NYC lawsuit resolution moved to outside_window; no cap needed.
